The letter came from a friend living overseas.
all: the whole quantity or extent of something
She spent all summer preparing for the entrance exam.
supports: gives help to, or provides evidence for
The new data supports the theory that sleep affects memory.
deserves: has earned something because of actions
Every child deserves a safe and loving home.
remembered: kept or brought back in the mind
The old teacher is still remembered fondly by his students.
novel: new and original; not existing before
The scientists proposed a novel method for storing solar energy.
consumed: used up, ate, or experienced something completely
The whole cake was consumed within minutes of the party starting.
afternoon: the time between noon and evening
We spent a lazy afternoon reading in the park.
largely: The delay was largely caused by bad weather conditions.
forgotten: The old recipe had been forgotten for nearly a century.
may: The meeting may be postponed if too few people attend.
done: Have you done your homework for tomorrow yet?
its: belonging to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
The cat licked its paw before curling up to sleep.
there: in, at, or to that place; used to show that something exists
There is a small cafe just around the corner.
also: The recipe also works well with chicken instead of beef.
limit: the greatest amount or extent allowed
There is a strict limit on how much luggage you can bring.
laboratory: a room or building used for scientific research or testing
The university built a new laboratory for its chemistry department.
transfers: present tense of transfer, used with he/she/it
Removing a link does not free up its share; it transfers the work to whoever is left.
recalling: the act of remembering something from the past
Recalling old memories often brings both comfort and sadness at once.
list: a set of items written one after another
She made a list of groceries before going to the market.
word: a single unit of language with a meaning
The English word salary is often said to come from payments made in salt.
pairs: sets of two things of the same kind
The students worked in pairs to complete the experiment.
reconstructing: building or forming an accurate picture of something again
Historians spent years reconstructing the events leading to the battle.
studies: pieces of research carried out to examine a subject in detail
Several studies confirm the benefits of regular exercise.
use: to employ something for a particular purpose
What cannot be coined is a reason to use them.
richer: having more depth, detail, or quality; more abundant
The revised course offers richer material for advanced students.
tend: to be likely to do or be something, usually
Older houses in this area tend to have thicker walls.
show: to prove or make clear that something is true
The results show that the new treatment is more effective.
smaller: less large in size, amount, or degree, compared with something else
This car is smaller than the one we had before.
real: actually existing; genuine, not imagined or fake
The documentary tells the real story behind the famous painting.
advantages: Living near the station has obvious advantages for daily commuters.
nor: used to introduce a second negative point after 'not'
She did not call, nor did she reply to any messages.
does: performs an action, or auxiliary form used in questions and negatives
She does her best to help everyone around her.
any: used to refer to one or some of a thing, no matter which
Do you have any questions before we begin the meeting?
mean: A red light at a crossing means drivers must stop.
twice: In a cold kitchen the dough may need twice that time to rise.
useless: not able to achieve anything useful; having no benefit
Reading twice is not useless, only far less useful than it feels.
only: and no one or nothing more besides; just
Only a handful of tickets remained by the time we arrived.
useful: able to be used effectively for a purpose; helpful
The useful question is not whether a task is hard, but whether anyone can say how it is done.
always: at all times; on every occasion
My grandmother always waters her plants early in the morning.
spent: past tense of spend: used time or money on something
He spent two hours fixing the broken fence yesterday.
follows: comes after something in time or order
A short quiz follows each chapter of the textbook.
practice: the actual doing of something, as opposed to theory
In practice, the new policy is harder to apply than expected.
modest: fairly small in size, amount, or degree
The company reported a modest increase in profits this quarter.
but: used to introduce something contrasting with what has just been said
She wanted to stay longer, but the last train was leaving soon.
awkward: There was an awkward silence after he forgot her name.
natural: existing in or produced by nature; not artificial
The spa uses only natural ingredients sourced from local farms.
before: earlier than a particular time or event
Please arrive at the airport before your flight is due to leave.
checking: the act of examining something to make sure it is correct
Checking the figures twice avoided an embarrassing mistake in the report.
last: coming after all others, or most recent
The last bus leaves the station at midnight.
section: a distinct part of something larger
The library's history section takes up an entire floor.
actually: in fact; really, contrary to what might be expected
The film was actually shot in a different country than the story suggests.
claimed: stated something as true, though it has not been proven
He claimed to have witnessed the entire accident firsthand.
leave: to go away from a place, or to allow something to remain
She will leave the office early to catch her train.
returning: Returning students often struggle to settle back into routine.
accept: to agree to take or receive something
The committee agreed to accept the proposal after minor revisions.
make: to produce, create or cause something
Good lighting can make a small room feel much larger.
return: the act of coming or going back
sự trở lại, sự trả lại
On his return, he found the house exactly as he left it.
unpleasant: not enjoyable or pleasing; causing discomfort
Leave a gap before returning, and accept that the gap will make the return unpleasant.
understand: to grasp the meaning or nature of something
The question sounds simple: do people understand less when they read on a screen?
nobody: not a single person; no one
Nobody expected the small team to win the championship.
reason: a cause or explanation for something
Nobody knew the real reason for his sudden resignation.
itself: used to refer back to a thing or situation already mentioned, for emphasis
The machine can clean itself without any help from a technician.
explains: makes something clear by describing it in detail
This explains why rereading notes feels productive but works so poorly.
methods: Farmers are adopting new methods to conserve water during droughts.
us: used to refer to the speaker and others, as the object
The line is drawn by biology, not by us.
failing: Despite failing twice, she kept trying until she passed.
fail: to not succeed at something attempted
Many new businesses fail within their first two years.
progress: forward movement towards a goal or improvement
The doctors were pleased with the patient's steady progress.
